business_summary: Apple designs and sells premium consumer hardware (iPhone, Mac, iPad, Watch, AirPods) and attaches a high-margin, recurring Services business (App Store, iCloud, Apple Music/TV+, AppleCare, advertising, search-licensing, payments) to the installed base. In fiscal Q3 2026 (quarter ended 2026-06-27) revenue was $109.417B, of which iPhone $54.252B (49.6%) and Services $30.739B (28.1%). The model: sell a device at a ~35-40% hardware margin, then earn a software-like recurring cut from the same customer for years. FY2026 has seen a sharp re-acceleration: 9-month revenue $364.357B, +16.2% vs $313.695B a year earlier. REFRESH 2026-10-28: no new filing since Q3 FY2026 - Q4 FY2026 results (and the FY2026 10-K) are due 2026-11-02 after the close, so the fundamentals below are unchanged and this refresh updates price, leadership, demand signals, regulation and consensus. New facts since the 2026-09-17 thesis: John Ternus became CEO on 2026-09-01 (Tim Cook is now executive chairman); the iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max launched at $1,199/$1,299 ($100 above predecessors) with the standard iPhone 18 deferred to spring; Nikkei reported (unconfirmed by Apple) 15-20% cuts to October Pro component orders, attributed to price increases driven by memory costs.

moat.type: Ecosystem switching costs + premium brand + installed-base network effect + extreme capital efficiency and silicon vertical integration

quality.revenue_growth_3y: ~6.8% CAGR from FY2023 ($383.285B) to TTM ended 2026-06-27 ($466.823B); most recent year +16.2% (9M FY2026 $364.357B vs 9M FY2025 $313.695B) - a sharp re-acceleration off a flat 2022-2024 base
quality.gross_margin: 48.7% TTM (gross profit $227.14B on revenue $466.823B, = Q4 FY2025 $48.341B + 9M FY2026 $178.8B); 50.1% in Q3 FY2026 but that included ~2pp of one-off tariff-refund benefit; company guided 47-48% for Q4 FY2026
quality.roic: ~67% TTM. NOPAT ~$127.6B (TTM operating income $154.83B x (1 - 17.6% effective tax rate)) over invested capital of ~$191.8B (shareholders' equity $107.5B + total term debt and commercial paper $84.3B). Excluding the $146.5B of cash and marketable securities the return on operating capital is far higher.
quality.net_debt_to_ebitda: negative - Apple is NET CASH by ~$62.2B ($146.517B cash + marketable securities vs $84.3B term debt + commercial paper at 2026-06-27). Ratio is not meaningful; balance-sheet risk is effectively nil.
quality.fcf_positive: yes; TTM free cash flow ~$136.7B (TTM operating cash flow $146.72B less capex $10.04B). 9M FY2026 alone: OCF $116.996B - capex $6.799B = $110.20B.

valuation.verdict: expensive - trading ~48% above our base fair value and ~25% above the high end of the band. Fair value is UNCHANGED from 2026-09-17 because no new filing has changed any input (per the 2026-09-17 playbook lesson, fair value only moves when a cited fundamental changes).
valuation.method: Blend of two methods via code/valuation.py (inputs unchanged from 2026-09-17; no new filing). (1) P/E: TTM diluted EPS $8.73 (Q4 FY2025 $1.85 + 9M FY2026 $6.88) x 24 / 28 / 33 -> $209.52 / $244.44 / $288.09. 28x base = Apple's 10-year median P/E of ~27.25x; 33x high allows for the growth re-acceleration; 24x low for a de-rating. (2) FCF yield: TTM FCF per diluted share $9.29 ($136.683B / 14.715B diluted shares) at 5.0% / 4.2% / 3.5% -> $185.80 / $221.19 / $265.43. Blended $197.66 / $232.82 / $276.76. At $344.70 the stock trades at 39.5x TTM EPS and a 2.70% TTM FCF yield. Forward sensitivity check (NOT used in the band, aggregator input): even on a forward FY2027 EPS of ~$9.57 (Barchart consensus as reported in search results, unverified) the 24/28/33x band is $229.68 / $267.96 / $315.81 - still below today's price.
valuation.trend: Price $344.70 (Alpaca bid 2026-10-28) is above its 50-day average ($331.77) and well above its 200-day average ($295.68); 250-day close range $246.72-$348.34 (high close 2026-10-22). Strong uptrend near all-time highs - momentum, not value, supports the price.

bull_case: Wide moat proven by pricing power: company gross margin 50.1% in Q3 FY2026 and 48.7% TTM - extraordinary for a business still ~74% hardware by revenue (TTM Products $346.3B of $466.8B).
Growth genuinely re-accelerated: 9M FY2026 revenue +16.2% YoY and 9M diluted EPS +22.4% ($6.88 vs $5.62), with iPhone +21.7% and Greater China +22.4% in Q3 FY2026.
Services is a $120.5B-TTM annuity (Q4 FY2025 $28.750B + 9M FY2026 $91.728B) growing ~14% at much higher margins than hardware.
Fortress balance sheet: ~$62.2B net cash, $138.0B of buyback authorization available, $62.1B repurchased in 9M FY2026; diluted shares shrinking ~2%/yr.
Capital-light cash machine: $136.7B TTM FCF on ~$10B capex; AI compute largely via partners (Google Gemini powers the revamped Siri).

Street still leans positive: 32 analysts rate it Moderate Buy (16 Buy / 12 Hold / 4 Sell) per TipRanks on 2026-10-26, and Q4 FY2026 consensus (~$1.99-2.00 EPS, ~$112.95B revenue) sits inside company guidance; Apple has beaten EPS consensus in 14 of the last 15 quarters (aggregator data).

Regulatory outcomes have so far been survivable: the Google search remedy (Sept 2025) still allows default-search payments to Apple (non-exclusive, reviewed yearly), and the December 2025 appeals ruling in Epic struck down the outright zero-commission ban on external purchases, leaving room for Apple to argue for some commission.
risks: VALUATION IS THE THESIS-KILLER. At $344.70 the stock is 39.5x TTM EPS and a 2.70% FCF yield vs a 10-year median P/E of ~27.25x. Price is ~48% above our base fair value ($232.82) and ~25% above our high case ($276.76). Even the analyst average 12-month target ($337.45, TipRanks 2026-10-26) is BELOW the current price.

iPhone 18 demand wobble: Nikkei (reported 2026-10-09, unconfirmed by Apple) said Apple cut October iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max component orders 15-20% vs initial plans, blamed on $100 higher prices ($1,199/$1,299) driven by memory-chip costs. UBS saw Pro wait times ~2 days shorter than a year ago across 30+ markets; JPMorgan's lead-time data was stronger. Signals are mixed, but this is the first crack in the supercycle narrative.

Deceleration and margin squeeze are now the bear base case among some analysts: Jefferies (Underperform, $270.62 target, 2026-10-26) expects December-quarter revenue +2% and EPS -4%, and FY2027 product gross margin down ~4pp with ~6% lower EPS; Morgan Stanley (Overweight, $355) still expects December-quarter guidance slightly below Street. KeyBanc is Underweight with a $250 target (2026-10-19).

Peak-earnings risk: Q3 FY2026's 50.1% gross margin included ~2pp (and $0.11 of EPS) of one-off tariff refunds; Q4 guide is 47-48% including ~1pp of refund benefit. The 10-Q warns component costs and supply constraints are expected 'to intensify' (advanced nodes, memory).

Leadership transition: John Ternus became CEO on 2026-09-01 after 15 years of Tim Cook. Cook stays as executive chairman, which lowers the risk, but the first CEO change since 2011 coincides with a product-cycle peak and an outsourced AI strategy - execution risk is non-zero.

Regulatory attack on the highest-margin revenue: EU DMA (EUR 500M fine under appeal; EU General Court confirmed gatekeeper designation; new lower EU commission terms from 2026-10-01); Epic contempt case before the US Supreme Court (argument expected this term, ruling likely by June 2027); DOJ March 2024 monopolization suit; DOJ cross-appeal seeking to ban Google's default-search payments to Apple (near-100%-margin revenue) is pending in the D.C. Circuit.

iPhone concentration (~50% of revenue) and cycle dependence; supercycles pull demand forward and create hard comparisons. The standard iPhone 18 was pushed to spring, which shifts revenue timing and muddies year-over-year comparisons.
AI dependence outsourced to Google Gemini - Apple rents rather than owns the key platform technology, deepening a relationship regulators are attacking.
Greater China ~17% of revenue ($18.816B of $109.417B in Q3 FY2026) plus heavy manufacturing exposure - standing geopolitical and tariff risk.
what_would_break_thesis: Company-wide gross margin falls below 44% for two consecutive quarters (48.7% TTM; Q4 FY2026 guidance 47-48%).
Total revenue shrinks year-over-year for two consecutive fiscal years.
Services revenue declines year-over-year for two consecutive quarters.
iPhone revenue declines year-over-year for three consecutive quarters, indicating the upgrade franchise - not just a cycle - has broken.
The ~$62.2B net cash position turns into net debt of more than 1.0x EBITDA.
TTM free cash flow falls below $90B (a ~35% drop from the current $136.7B).

A final, non-appealable regulatory or court outcome that forces Apple to give up its App Store commission on a material share of transactions, or that ends the Google search-licensing payments, without an offsetting replacement.
Annual buybacks fall below $40B while the balance sheet still holds net cash.
Any serious accounting red flag, restatement, or auditor change.

PRICE DISCIPLINE (entry rule, not a sell rule): do not initiate or add above $233 (base fair value). A first tranche is only justified below ~$210 (roughly 10% under base). Re-check this after the 2026-11-02 Q4 FY2026 report.
catalysts: Q4 FY2026 results and FY2026 10-K on 2026-11-02 after the close (CEO Ternus and CFO Parekh) - the single most important datapoint: does growth land at 9-11% and gross margin at 47-48% ex the fading tariff benefit, and what is the December-quarter guide given the iPhone 18 Pro order-cut reports? This thesis MUST be refreshed with the new filing by 2026-11-04.
A pullback into the $200-$233 zone - the only thing that makes this ownable; requires a ~32-43% decline from $344.70.
Spring 2027 launch of the standard iPhone 18 and the foldable; Gemini-powered Siri adoption.
Supreme Court argument/decision in Apple v. Epic (ruling likely by June 2027) and the D.C. Circuit decision on the DOJ cross-appeal over Google default-search payments.
A broad market or rate-driven de-rating of mega-cap multiples.
